questions.question: Q1 Which etching mode produced an isotropic profile in the simulation?

explanations.a: Correct! Wet etching produced isotropic undercutting.
explanations.d: One mode clearly produced isotropic behavior.

questions.question: Q2 Which etching mode produced vertical sidewalls?

explanations.b: Correct! Dry plasma etching creates anisotropic profiles.
explanations.c: Only dry etching does this effectively.

questions.question: Q3 What happened when acid concentration was increased?

explanations.a: Correct! Higher concentration increased chemical activity.

questions.question: Q4 What happened when RF power was increased?

explanations.a: Correct! Higher RF power strengthens plasma activity.

questions.question: Q5 Which layer remained protected during etching?

explanations.a: Correct! The photoresist masked the protected regions.
explanations.d: The chamber is not a wafer layer.

questions.question: Q6 Why was photoresist stripped after etching?

answers.a: Its job as a mask was complete

explanations.a: Correct! The masking function was no longer required.

questions.question: Q7 What is a common disadvantage of wet etching?

explanations.a: Correct! Wet etching can remove material sideways.
explanations.d: Vertical profiles are harder with wet etching.

questions.question: Q8 What is a major advantage of dry etching?

explanations.a: Correct! Dry etching provides excellent anisotropic control.

questions.question: Q9 Which process output indicates the speed of material removal?

explanations.a: Correct! Etch rate measures removal speed.
explanations.b: Yield quality is a performance metric.

questions.question: Q10 Which etching technique is generally preferred for modern nanoscale fabrication?

explanations.a: Correct! Modern fabrication requires precise anisotropic control.
explanations.b: Wet etching is less precise for nanoscale structures.
explanations.d: Used for planarization, not pattern transfer.
